metadata.purpose: PRI MLP training and validation only; held-out test rows are intentionally excluded.
metadata.split_policy: original attack train/val splits preserved; benign utility data are stratified by dataset category/type

MT-Bench.selection: stratified by category; first 5 questions per category; both turns included
MT-Bench.held_out_for_utility_evaluation: remaining 5 questions per category, 80 turns total

XSTest.split: safe prompts only; stratified by safe type

OR-Bench-Hard-1K.split: stratified by category; deterministic first rows within each category

def longest_common_subsequence(X , Y): 
    # Find lengths of two strings 
    m = len(X) 
    n = len(Y) 
  
    # Create a table to store results of sub-problems 
    dp = [[None]*(n+1) for i in range(m+1)] 
  
    # Fill dp[][] in bottom up manner 
    for i in range(1, m+1): 
        for j in range(1, n+1): 
            if X[i-1] == Y[j-1]: 
                dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]+1
            else: 
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]) 
  
    return dp[m][n]
```
